notes: The Skerrow's high roads and passes (docs/WORLD_LIFE_ROADS.md). Clanless and the Unroped at the passes and bridges, scree-hags on the gorge sides, crag-wolves and a stone-thrall crossing at night; on the road by day the clans' own traffic: memory-keepers walking to the Moot, Rudd carrying blood-price to the Stones, Skarl drovers, a tinker off the Oskel Edge camp. Caravans: Kharrow's pack train to Ruddow, Brindlecrag's ore carts to the Hold, and a Skarl pack train down from Skarlow.

name: Clanless in the rocks
notes: The clanless who ride for Corbie Stack let a body pass who has paid the black-rent at the Pillar (core:dialogue/black_rent_pillar_basket).

lines.speaker: A clanless raider
lines.spring: No clan, no toll-stone, no mercy.

name: The Unroped's price
notes: Old Ghastow's people out on the road. The bait is one of them, a broken chain round his neck, who asks what you owe.

folk.name: A man with a broken chain

talk.prompt: Ask the man with the broken chain what he wants

lines.speaker: One of the Unroped
lines.spring: What are you worth? Nobody? Then nobody's owed for you.

name: Stones from above
notes: Scree-hags on the gorge side: the stones come first, from above, to find out whether you are the sort who looks up.

lines.speaker: A scree-hag
lines.spring: Look up. Look up. Look up.

name: A thrall carrying
notes: A stone-thrall crossing the road in the dark with a bone in its arms, going toward the Sorting Ground; it wants to be let past.

talk.prompt: Walk a way with the memory-keeper
talk.say: I am walking the Rope-Song to the Moot. Every verse, every name in it, from the Dreugh door to the Skarl fold. You may walk with me for a verse or two, if you do not talk. — There is a place up there the song goes quiet over. Go and look at it, if you like. I will not.

hook.rumour: The memory-keeper's song went quiet over {place}.

name: Blood-price on the road
notes: Two Rudd carrying a clan's blood-price to the Stones on the North Road, in plain sight, as the law says it is paid.

talk.prompt: Ask the Rudd what they carry
talk.say: A death's price, to the Stones, on the road where everyone can see. That is the point of the road. — Nine head and a year's peat, the reckoner said. We are carrying the coin for the peat. The beasts are walking on their own, behind, slower.

hook.rumour: The price-bearers came from the reckoner at {place}.

talk.say: Down the dale, and they know the way better than I do. Stand still till they're past, they don't like strangers standing in the middle of their road. — If you're going up Skarldale, water at the drove-well and ring the bell. Everything round there knows that note.
Mended pots, mended chains, mended news. The news is the dear one.

name: A kite on the road
notes: An Oskel kite-boy whose hawk-kite has come down across the road; helping him get it up again reveals the Kite-Watch.

talk.prompt: Help the boy with his kite
talk.say: It came down in a gust, right across the road, and the line's fouled on the stones. Hold the drum, would you, and walk back when I say. — There! There she goes. Runa'll skin me if she sees it dipping; dipping means riders. She flies the big ones at the Kite-Watch, out west. Go and see them, they're grand.

name: A coffin going up
notes: Skarl bearers walking a coffin up to the Breath-Ledge; they tell you why and the Ledge is found.

talk.say: Old Brenna. Taking her up to the Ledge, to Mags, to be hung as high as the rope goes. Nearest the mouth goes first, and she'd want to be first, she always was. — You can walk with us a bit. Don't help carry. It's ours to carry.

hook.rumour: The bearers were taking a coffin up to {place}.

name: A rent-rider
notes: One of Annet Blackrent's collectors on foot, polite and unarmed by his own account, reminding the road of the black-rent; reveals the Black-Rent Pillar.

talk.say: No horse? No farm either, then, and nothing for me. — If you ever have a roof below the passes, the basket's on the Pillar by the Rudd road. Put in what's fair and haul it up. It's cheaper than a new barn. Annet says to tell everybody that, nicely.

hook.rumour: The rent-rider spoke of the basket on {place}.

name: Skeps to the heather
notes: At dusk, when the bees are in, a clan's bee-keepers carry their skeps up to the heather on poles; they share a comb and send you to the Bee-Bole Crag.

talk.say: Going up to the heather while it's in flower; the bees are in for the night and they'll not mind the carrying if you don't jog them. Here, take a bit of last year's. — Ours winter at the Bee-Bole Crag with everybody's, a row a clan. Bannoch keeps them. Don't take from the boles without asking him.

hook.rumour: The bee-keepers keep their skeps at {place}.

name: A disputed claim
notes: Two prospectors, Brindle and Kharrow, at the road's edge with stakes and a vein between them, each waiting for a witness; speaking to them settles it the Moot's way and points to the Scour.

talk.say: You'll do for a witness, you're nobody's. He staked it at noon; I staked it at noon. — Halves, then, the Moot's way, and the witness says so. Right. Done. — If you want to see a vein that nobody can argue over, go up to the Scour and watch Wat Hobb pull his sluice. If he ever does.

hook.rumour: The prospectors spoke of the hushing-dam at {place}.

name: Annet's riders
notes: Somebody took the black-rent out of the basket on the Pillar (core:dialogue/black_rent_pillar_basket): Annet Blackrent's riders are on the roads looking for who.

lines.speaker: One of Annet's riders
lines.spring: That was Hobb's rent you took out of the basket. Hobb's barn burned for it. Your turn.
